final_candidates.decision_summary: ESM-1v strongly supports Q63E (z=0.615) and E63 appears in ~10% of homologs, indicating evolutionary tolerance. A negative charge near the basic region can modulate TAR-binding without disrupting the transactivation core.
K→R preserves positive charge in the essential RKKRR basic domain with modest PLM support. Weak homolog tolerance (~2%) limits confidence but functional charge-preservation logic supports retention.
Y47H introduces a protonatable histidine adjacent to the basic domain with plausible ESM-1v support. Low homolog frequency of H (~2%) argues it is not an evolutionarily favored solution.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool has converged after two evidence rounds; remaining tools are either not applicable or would return identical cached evidence.

history.rationale: Position 47 sits at the start of the Arg-rich core/basic domain; a His substitution retains positive charge and may fine-tune TAR RNA binding affinity while preserving overall charge distribution.
Core domain aromatic position; His may retain intercalation into TAR base triple while adding pH-tunable interaction. Needs PLM and MSA validation.
Biological prior for Tyr47His in the core transactivation domain is strong, but ESM-1v plausibility is near zero (0.008). Keep but lower rank; sequence prior conflicts with functional prior.
Y47H gains a protonatable histidine adjacent to the basic domain but homologs rarely carry H (2%), arguing it is not an evolutionary favored solution. Demoted below K51R.
Conservative swap within the RKKRRQRRR basic domain that maintains RNA-binding cationic character and is a naturally tolerated exchange in lentiviral Tat homologs.
Basic region residue contacting TAR phosphate backbone; Arg extends reach and often strengthens RNA binding. Conservative substitution with plausible gain.

Conservative basic-domain substitution with a plausible functional rationale (enhanced TAR/arginine chemistry), despite weak ESM-1v support (0.002); model prior is weak for arginine-rich motifs, so discount it.

K→R preserves positive charge in the essential RKKRR basic domain and has good PLM support, but homolog frequency of R at 51 is only ~2%, indicating weak evolutionary tolerance. Retain as rank 2 given functional logic of charge preservation.
Within the acidic activation/PVDPRLEPW region; added positive charge near the activation domain boundary may strengthen LTR coactivator interactions without disrupting essential acidic residues.
Acidic-proximal region; phosphorylation at nearby Ser/Thr modulates transactivation, but direct gain here is speculative.
Near-zero ESM-1v plausibility and phosphorylation-site disruption in the acidic N-terminal region likely harms transactivation.

rejection.reason: Near-zero ESM-1v plausibility and phosphorylation-site disruption in the acidic N-terminal region likely harms transactivation.

history.rationale: Conservative lysine substitution in the core RKKRRQRRR motif preserves TAR-binding charge while slightly altering side-chain flexibility, potentially improving binding kinetics.
R53 is deeply conserved in the arginine-rich motif; Lys may weaken the critical nucleotide-base contact. Lowered pending evidence.
Moderate ESM-1v plausibility (0.043) and a conservative R->K in the core arginine-rich region; retained but below the functional candidates.
Despite ~6% homolog tolerance, ESM-1v plausibility is near-zero and R53 sits in the core RKKRR motif where weakening arginine fidelity risks reduced TAR binding. Safer to reject in favor of K51R.

rejection.reason: Despite ~6% homolog tolerance, ESM-1v plausibility is near-zero and R53 sits in the core RKKRR motif where weakening arginine fidelity risks reduced TAR binding. Safer to reject in favor of K51R.

history.rationale: Core-region proline could rigidify the kink between cysteine-rich and basic domains, a conformational feature important for TAR recognition.
Proline in the flexible linker may disrupt transactivation conformation; low prior.
Proline insertion in the essential helical core region has near-zero plausibility and high risk of disrupting the transactivation domain.

rejection.reason: Proline insertion in the essential helical core region has near-zero plausibility and high risk of disrupting the transactivation domain.

history.rationale: End of the conserved Cys-rich FHCQVCF motif; histidine at this position occurs in some HIV-1 variants and may improve stability of the Zn-coordination-like core.
Alternative to Y47H at the core try stack; keep as comparitor pending ESM-1v scoring.
Loss of the conserved aromatic Phe in the core domain is poorly supported (0.0001) and likely destabilizing to TAR interaction.

rejection.reason: Loss of the conserved aromatic Phe in the core domain is poorly supported (0.0001) and likely destabilizing to TAR interaction.

history.rationale: Second turret candidate in the HQNSQ stretch; glutamate substitutions here are associated with increased processive transcription in literature on Tat turret mutations.
Gln-rich region affects transactivation; charge change is speculative.

ESM-1v gives by far the strongest plausibility (0.615) among all candidates, and it is a conservative substitution in the variable second exon/regulatory region. Raise confidence, but phenotype is not directly measured.

E63 is present in ~10% of homologs and ESM-1v strongly supports the substitution (z=0.615); a negative charge near the basic region can modulate TAR-binding affinity without core disruption. Best combined evidence across tools.
Another conservative basic-domain exchange; preserves arginine-guanidinium chemistry only partially, so lower prior on net gain.
Similar concern as R53K; RKKRR motif is highly conserved for TAR binding.
Weakening a key arginine in the RKKRR core with K is riskier than K51R and has no PLM support.

rejection.reason: Weakening a key arginine in the RKKRR core with K is riskier than K51R and has no PLM support.

history.rationale: Removes a phosphorylation-acceptor Thr near the cysteine-rich domain that could reduce negative regulation by host kinases, a plausible but speculative gain.
Cysteine-cluster region T23 is far from known transactivation determinants; low relevance.
Cysteine-region-adjacent Thr to Ala offers no transactivation benefit and near-zero model support.

rejection.reason: Cysteine-region-adjacent Thr to Ala offers no transactivation benefit and near-zero model support.
